messages:
tara_cs: Heads-up: ran a quick audit and found ~60 accounts where playbook notes were attributed to the wrong owner after last night's owner-sync.

tara_cs: example: ACCT-5512 shows owner = 'jordan_old' in notes but account.owner = 'zara_enablement'. notes contain 'Onboard: resources sent' and were created at ~2025-06-18T03:04Z.

mike_data: that sounds like a join order bug in the sync job. can you paste the SQL you used?

tara_cs: ```SELECT n.account_id, n.owner, a.owner as current_owner, count(*) FROM notes n JOIN accounts a ON n.account_id = a.id WHERE n.created_at >= '2025-06-18' AND n.body LIKE '%Onboard: resources sent%' GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING n.owner <> a.owner;```

ops-bot: alert: owner-sync v3 completed 2025-06-18T02:58:12Z; rows processed=12789; warnings=3.

leo_eng: quick root cause theory: owner-sync emits two events per change for legacy crm records; playbook runner subscribes and attributes note.owner based on event.payload.previous_owner when a race occurs. i'll take a look at the consumer.

mike_data: can we rollback? i don't want incorrect owner attribution affecting healthscore and auto-renew nudges.

tara_cs: can we at least stop playbook from creating owner-assigned notes until we fix attribution? maybe set notes.owner=null for playbook runs or pause the specific operator.

leo_eng: temporary mitigation: set rule flag `assign_owner_from_event=false` for rules tagged with 'onboard' via ops endpoint. curl: `POST /ops/playbook/config` body `{ "filter": "tags:onboard", "patch": {"assign_owner_from_event": false} }`

zara_enablement: API to patch configs requires svc-token. can ops team apply? also exporting affected accounts with current owner mismatch and renewal buckets would help prioritization.

mike_data: will run export now and attach to the thread. fields: account_id,current_owner,notes_owner,count,renewal_days. running query and pushing CSV to s3://cs-exports/owner_mismatch_6143219999.csv

ops-bot: export job completed: s3://cs-exports/owner_mismatch_6143219999.csv (61 rows)

zara_enablement: thanks. of those, how many are within renewal windows (<90d)? we should tag high-touch.

mike_data: quick counts: 9 <90d, 2 <30d. adding column 'high_touch' and updating the CSV.

leo_eng: i've opened a small change to playbook runner to prefer current account.owner over event.previous_owner when present. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8391. will patch config after ops toggles flag.

tara_cs: ops toggled flag for onboard-tagged rules; confirmed via `GET /ops/playbook/config?tags=onboard` returning assign_owner_from_event=false.

zara_enablement: i'll assign the 11 high-touch accounts to enablement reps and run a quick outreach template. adding to enablement standup at 11:15.

leo_eng: rolling fix to staging now, adding unit test to ensure notes use account.owner if available. will monitor for any further mismatches.

mike_data: once fix is prod, i'll run a backfill to correct notes.owner where it differs and add audit reason 'owner-sync-mismatch-6143219999'. planning after change window.

ops-bot: scheduled backfill job 2025-06-18T10:00Z, ETA rows fixed=61.

tara_cs: solid. thanks team. tagging this for postmortem; suggest adding an alert in the healthscore pipeline for owner drift >5% within 24h.
